messages:
talia: Noticed connection count creeping up in our overnight soak on Pixel 5A. Using Retrofit + OkHttp on Android 12. Backgrounding app + toggling wifi reproduces it. Has anyone seen leaking idle sockets during doze?

juan: Yep. On some devices the cleanup ScheduledExecutor for ConnectionPool doesn't run while the CPU is suspended, so idle sockets stick around.

kai: Also check our coroutine adapter. If cancellation isn't propagated immediately to OkHttp Call, callbacks can still run and keep connections referenced.

talia: We already call call.cancel in invokeOnCancellation but still see callbacks after cancel. Logs:

```
I/OkHttp: ConnectionPool: total=14 idle=14
W/OkHttp: Socket closed during keepalive check
E/Network: Read failed: socket was closed
```

juan: Two approaches that helped in other apps: 1) schedule a lightweight health ping on resume to re-establish good sockets, 2) on connectivity flaps, run connectionPool.evictAll() but guarded by an error threshold to avoid reconnect storms.

kai: I opened a small change that adds a cancel-guard boolean in the callback path so once we cancel we ignore late responses instead of re-issuing follow-ups. Also added a debug flag to trigger a forced cleanup in tests. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2533

talia: Can we add a tiny emulator sample in devex/samples that toggles network and asserts pool size bounded? CI should catch regressions then.

android-ci-bot: CI build for PR 2533 started on android-integration-tests (artifact: 8.4.0-beta).

juan: I'll add the sample and a resilience test that tolerates a small number of flaps. We should avoid evictAll on every event.

talia: Thanks. Action items: @juan add emulator sample + integration test; @kai land cancel-guard + test hook. We'll monitor Dedicated mobile soak after rollout. :thumbsup:
